content.title: Orlando Magic vs. Charlotte Hornets: Game Preview | Orlando Magic
content.text: ORLANDO – Throughout the season, terms like do-or-die and must win are assigned to games.While in some instances it’s clear hyperbole, tonight those words fully apply.The Orlando Magic (45-37) will attempt to extend their season and punch their ticket to the playoffs when they host the Charlotte Hornets (44-38) in a win-or-go-home play-in matchup on Friday at 7:30 p.m. ET. The contest will air exclusively on Prime Video.“I expect everybody to leave it all out there,” said Magic guard Desmond Bane. “Tomorrow is not promised. I don’t think anyone wants the season to come to an end. You’ve got to play your best when it matters. Go and try and win a game.”Orlando has been in its share of pressure-packed outings over the course of the 2025-26 campaign. The Magic played in 43 clutch contests during the regular season and earned 27 victories in those meetings – tied for the most in the NBA with the Detroit Pistons.“We have a great history of being in these situations and figuring it out,” said Magic center Wendell Carter Jr. “Now that we’re here, it’s time to make the most of it. The biggest thing going into this game is after it, we don’t want anyone to come back into that locker room saying, ‘I could have played harder.’ We’re going to make and miss shots. That comes with the game. But in terms of playing hard, that should not be a question going into tonight.”The Magic are well aware of the threat posed by the Hornets. Charlotte went 3-1 against Orlando this season, winning the final three matchups by an average of 20.3 points per game. The Magic will look to combat that tonight by establishing their presence on both ends of the floor.“You don’t win the game in the first quarter, but you set the tone,” said Bane. “We’ve got to come out and set the tone … (That tone is) physicality. That’s been our bread and butter. That’s who we are.”Charlotte was one of the league’s best teams down the stretch, winning 18 of their final 25 matchups.As a unit, the Hornets do plenty of damage to their opponents from beyond the arc. Charlotte is just the fourth team in NBA history with a trio of players to make at least 200 3-pointers in a season (LaMelo Ball, Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel). Ball and Knueppel are also just the second pair of teammates in league history to each record 260 triples made in a season, joining Golden State’s Stephen Curry and Klay Thompson, who accomplished the feat four times.“They made a lot of threes in (our matchups with them),” said Carter. “That’s the biggest thing. We’ve got to do a better job of eliminating that. Taking that out of the game and making it a grind-it-out win … We’ve got to get them off the 3-point line. That’s the No. 1 thing on the bulletin board.”PLAYOFF PICTURE: As mentioned, the winner of tonight’s play-in game between Orlando and Charlotte will be the East’s No. 8 seed in the playoffs and take on Detroit in the first round. Regardless of who advances from the play-in, Game 1 in Detroit will be Sunday at 6:30 p.m. and will air on NBC/Peacock.IN AND OUT: Jonathan Isaac (left knee; sprain) is questionable for Orlando.For Charlotte, Moussa Diabate (left hip; soreness) is questionable.QUOTES TO NOTE: “We need them. They’ve been there all year supporting us. This is their chance to come loud and proud and support the group. We’ve been fighting, we’ve been scratching (and) we’ve been clawing. We’re going to need everyone on our team, but also everybody in the city to rally behind us (and) to help us go get it done.” – Bane on the fan support at Kia Center“Stay in the present moment. If you look in the past, you get stuck there. Our guys need to have the ability to stay in the moment, and that’s what they’ve done. They’ve proven in moments like this, (high pressure games), that they can perform.” – Magic head coach Jamahl MosleyHOW TO WATCH: Watch the contest on Prime Video.
